text.p: Here are the highlights of stories in the Danish press on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

--Danish pharmaceuticals and biotechnology group Novo Nordisk sees possibility of more efficient medicine production after Scottish scientists cloned the lamb dubbed Polly in recent transgenetic experiments. Novo has a 13 percent shareholding in PPL Therapeutics, the firm behind the latest cloning operation at Edinburgh's Rosslin Institute.
--Danish banks are headed for record first-half 1997 profits due to increased earnings from securities and loans. Mid-August sees the beginning of the corporate half-year result season in Denmark.
--The Scandinavian Tobacco Company, which has a near monopoly on cigarette sales in Denmark, says it does not fear the European Union's looming ban on smoking advertising.

--The internal dispute within the far-left opposition Socialist Peoples Party (SF) over whether or not to recommend a "yes" or "no" to June's Amsterdam Treaty on EU reforms, roars on. There is deep dissatisfaction in the party about the split between leader Holger Nielsen's rejectionist line and prominent leadership figures' positive stance. Denmark is to hold a referendum on the treaty next year.
--Copenhagen International Airport may be forced by EU airport taxation harmonisation plans to raise its prices.

--Leading members of SF accuse party leader Holger Nielsen of adopting "Stalinist" methods in trying to force party members in favour of the EU's Amsterdam Treaty to adopt his rejectionist line and advocate a "no" in next year's Europe vote in Denmark.
--Danish shares are still relatively cheap despite recent rises and it is not too late to jump on the stock bandwagon as bond yields remain low.
